description: This role focused on developing and deploying computer vision systems for automated quality inspection in automotive manufacturing lines. I contributed across the entire development pipeline, from designing vision panels and collecting data to training models, configuring lighting, developing user interfaces, and installing and validating hardware on-site. This work sits at the intersection of computer vision, mechatronics, and manufacturing engineering to improve reliability and efficiency in industrial automation.

This research focused on developing lead-free piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENG) with greater piezoelectric coefficients for more efficient energy harvesting. We planned to achieve this by doping and growing Zinc Oxide NanoWires in our lab to improve their piezoelectric properties. This field of research intersects materials science, mechatronics, and chemistry to drive innovations in sustainable energy solutions.

company: Bazylak Group and Latner Thoracic Research Laboratories
description: Optimized a MATLAB pipeline for extracting lung vasculature and airway geometry, achieving a 47% reduction in processing time using memory allocation techniques and MATLAB Profiler tools. Developed mouse lung airway imaging methods producing micro-CT scans with over 1,000 airway branches (~30 generations) and constructed simplified airway geometries for CFD analysis using the Branch Builder tool.

Engaged in the design, fabrication, and testing of airframe components, including the shell, wings, and motor mount for drone in the Aerial Evolution Association of Canada UAS competition. Facilitated manufacturing of components using various techniques including 3D printing, carbon fiber, fiberglass, and epoxy resin to optimize weight and structural integrity.

Contributed to the production of Bombardier Global Express 5000 wings and center fuselage, ensuring compliance with quality standards. Performed tasks such as painting touchups, cleaning, sandblasting, and preparing wings for leak tests across multiple production stages, including spar shop, final inspection, and shipping preparation.

As an Undergraduate Researcher participating in the Faculty of Applied Sciences and Engineering Undergraduate Summer Research Program (FASE USRP), I volunteered as a judge for the UofT Discovery Symposium where High School students presented posters about research they conducted in the UofT Discovery program.

Supported event setup, cleanup, and food and beverage service to ensure smooth operations and a positive guest experience. Assisted attendees with concerns, provided prompt solutions, and communicating with colleagues to maintain high quality service.
